recat.why: the 762 event is the founding of the Abbasid imperial capital — a power moment. Its 'sci' tag comes from the golden-age tail welded into the title; as sci it either folds confusingly into Essentials (me-sci has only 2 members, under FACET_MIN) or, once a real Science facet exists, would strip the golden age out of Essentials entirely. Recat to power keeps the moment in Essentials; the science story belongs to a proper golden-age episode in sci (see flags).

reimp.why: the single biggest transformation of the region — one century turns the Mideast and North Africa from Roman/Persian/Christian/Zoroastrian into the Arab-Islamic world. Any one-page history names it; imp 2 puts it at LESS in the Wars facet where it lives.

the Scramble for Africa is the turning point of the continent's modern history — a one-page Africa history names the partition. At imp 3, LESS currently shows nothing of Africa after the pyramids except the slave-trade ribbon.

decolonization is the counterpart turning point to the partition — a third of the world's states date from this decade. One-page tier, and pairs with Berlin 1884 so LESS tells the whole colonial arc, not half of it.

the moment the Arab world becomes Ottoman for four centuries and the caliphate moves to Istanbul — a bigger change than its imp-4 peers (Kadesh, Cape Colony). Solidly 'what a course would cover'; stays NORMAL, ranks above regional detail.

peak 8 puts six centuries of tri-continental superpower in the same tier as Assyria and a rung BELOW the 89-year Umayyad caliphate (9). By the file's own 'how big did this ever get' scale the Ottomans at 1550-1680 belong in the >=9 tier with Achaemenid Persia and the Abbasids.

flags.issue: THE FOUNDER'S NAMED MISS, and it is structural, not a category error: the spread is already kind=technology -> cat sci (SPREADCAT in relations.ts), but layers.ts build() counts me-sci at only 2 members (this spread + one event), under FACET_MIN=4, so no me-sci layer is created and layerIdFor() folds the 5,000-year level-1 Writing ribbon into me-ess — exactly what the founder is seeing. Fix in layers.ts (exempt lvl-1/2 spreads from the footnote fold, or lower FACET_MIN for sci) and/or grow the ME science corpus: the alphabet (Phoenicia), Egyptian mathematics/medicine, al-Khwarizmi's algebra, the House of Wisdom, African ironworking would give the facet real members. Do NOT lower the spread's weight to hide it — peak 9.8 is honest.

double-barrelled title welds a 762 founding moment to a 500-year intellectual era. Recat to power proposed above; the golden age itself deserves its own sci episode/era (~750-1258, House of Wisdom to the Mongol sack), which would also give me-sci a real member.

self-described 'composite ribbon for the European partition' — it is not a polity and its from/to lineage semantics are fiction. Deliberate per its note, but the honest shape is an era-kind spread; as a polity it draws as a peak-7 'empire' named Colonial Africa in the States & empires layer.

an archaeological culture, not a state or polity; no ruler, border or lineage. Peak 1 hides it below DETAILED anyway — either move it to a sci/art context (earliest West African ironworking and sculpture) or accept it as a category stretch.

weight curve ends RISING: [-525,2],[-30,4] has Ptolemaic Egypt climbing to 4 at the moment Rome absorbs it. Late Ptolemaic Egypt was a declining client state; the -30 value looks like a typo or a misplaced Cleopatra-era bump — the curve should fall to ~1-2 at -30.

no event marks the Ottoman collapse and WWI partition of the Middle East (1918-1923, mandates/Sykes-Picot) — the origin of the entire modern map — and nothing marks the Iranian Revolution (1979). NORMAL cannot show 'the biggest changes' of the 20th-century Mideast with a blank between Berlin 1884 and Israel 1948; the polity ribbons (ottoman ends 1922, turkey/iran start) carry it only implicitly.
